status: draft, 2026-10-09: generated and checked offline against the canonical heightmap; not applied to any world, not seen in game
request: the owner, 2026-10-09: "MUSHROOM ISLAND: foliage and life. It is empty." Mushroom Island is the Fungal Isle (data/regions.json fungal_isle: fungal_north and fungal_south, cell F1, 0.77 km2, painted minecraft:mushroom_fields over MYCELIUM with 4% small red and brown mushrooms and nothing else).
generated_by: hand. tools/fungal_isle.py reads this file and the canonical heightmap and writes the pack, the Habitat Block and pool records (records --write) and the presence probes (probes --write). Nothing in it is read from a world.
built_by: tools/fungal_isle.py; builder's tests tests/test_fungal_isle.py (not an independent audit). Design note: docs/world-building/FUNGAL_ISLE.md.
what_it_is_not: Not a foliage-model change. data/foliage.json feeds the WorldPainter export (tools/paint_maps.py); the world is already exported and a pre-exported world never regenerates, so a fungal_wood type there would reach only a future re-export, and would move the canopy hash data/visibility.json was measured on. The live world gets blocks only through a re-apply step, so this file owns the island's growth.

Not Grandmother Cap's ring. The fairy ring at (608, 5888) is data/southern_residents.json fairy_ring (R9SR, R18SR) and stands untouched; this file keeps 30 blocks clear of it and builds three different places.

Not idle scenery Pokemon. tools/ambient_idle.py is a town model (town plans, derived/ plans, a cap per town); the only wild-site seam is a place module exposing idlers() the way tools/pokemon_farm.py does, which cannot be exercised without derived/ and is left alone. The island's visible life is the three activated Habitat Blocks below plus the existing sub-region rosters (data/spawns.json fungal_north, fungal_south).
ground_rule: Every Y is round(ground) from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap). Nothing here reads a world save. Paint is a fill ... replace minecraft:mycelium over a slab, so it follows the terrain without being told its height and changes no column's height.

build.note: A pure block pass: no load or tick function, nothing that runs unless called, so a server pack and not world-local. Run BEFORE R9E: the three Habitat Blocks stand in blocks this pack writes (their mimic is the block written there).

rules.shore_clear_why: no written column within 22 blocks (horizontally) of a column at or under y64: a cap is up to 12 blocks across and the sea bar chain (data/water_shape.json fungal_bar_chain) works on the coast
rules.max_slope_deg_why: the island's slope p90 is 26.2 degrees (data/regions.json fungal_isle.measured.slope_degrees), all of it at the coast; above this a stem stands on a face

the east-coast storm tower, template cobbleverse:legendary/zapdos, size [31, 66, 29] at its corner

rules.glade_scatter_margin_why: the scatter keeps a glade's own radius plus this clear, so a glade reads as a room in the island's growth and the two never write one block

blocks.why: every id a vanilla 1.21.1 block and none a spawn-condition block but water, the Glowcap Hollow's pool, which data/spawn_block_policy.json whitelists for fungal_isle with the risk stated (data/spawn_blocks.json, checked on every build). No concrete (contract C4). The glowing blocks are shroomlight (Cap Wood's beacon) and the two froglights (the Glowcap Hollow); no oak leaves, spore blossom or flowering azalea, which the spawn policy names.

scatter.scale_why: island-wide growth: the objects every wood is made of, laid by the same density method tools/foliage.py uses (its noise() and Spacing, imported, not copied): clumping noise at 72 blocks, glades at 320, minimum spacing between every pair of stems, bigger classes first
scatter.edge_ramp_why: density rises from nothing at shore_clear to full 90 blocks inland, so the coast stays a beach and the middle is a wood

giants.why: the skyline: a red spotted dome, a brown umbrella or a stack of tiers on one stem, 10 to 22 blocks of stem under a cap 9 to 16 across

mediums.why: the understory: a person-high cap you walk under

stumps.why: dark oak stumps with shelf fungi (brown and red caps) growing from the sides: what the island's old trees left

logs.why: fallen dark oak logs with moss on top and a bracket on the side

tufts.why: clusters of small red and brown mushrooms on a patch of podzol, the way the plant layer's 4% never grouped them

paint.why: podzol under a giant's stem to its cap's radius plus 1, moss on the next 2 blocks; the Cap Wood and the hollow carry their own

glades.name: The Cap Wood
glades.memorable: the tallest thing on the island: one 30-block stem under a 24-block red cap with a ring of shroomlight hung from its underside, in a clearing ringed by seven elder caps, then a wood. Lit at night from below, seen from the whole north plateau.
glades.why_here: the north heart's focus is (432, 5488) radius 112 (data/encounter_design.json fungal_north.heart: 'the middle of the mushroom island, where the caps grow tallest'); the clearing is 90 blocks from it on the flattest ground nearest (relief 0.7 over a 49-block box, measured 2026-10-09 on tools/ground.py), where the stem stands level

glades.name: The Stump Court
glades.memorable: a bare, trodden dojo floor in the middle of the growth: a great cut stump with its rings showing, fourteen smaller stumps round it, every one with shelf fungi, and six brown umbrellas leaning round the edge like an audience.
glades.why_here: the central plateau, ground 145 with relief 1.0 over 49 blocks; 176 blocks from Grandmother Cap's ring, 218 from the Cap Wood

glades.name: The Glowcap Hollow
glades.memorable: a sunken hollow forty blocks across and nine deep with a pool at the bottom and a cold purple-and-green light coming up out of it: stems topped with froglight caps on the slopes, buds round the water, a rim of ordinary caps hiding it until you stand over it. The island's fungal pools.
glades.why_here: data/encounter_design.json fungal_south names a water_body 'fungal_pools' that no landmark or water mask defines (the island is entirely dry: 0 of 12,061 sampled columns wet) and a water table (Tadbulb, Dewpider, Araquanid) with nowhere to spawn; this makes the pool. 48 blocks from the south heart's focus (592, 6000), 80 from Grandmother Cap's ring
